headline: A huge typhoon forces a million people from their homes

sources.title: More than 1.7 million evacuated as Typhoon Bavi makes landfall in China
Typhoon Bavi makes landfall in eastern China as more than 1 million are evacuated
China evacuates over one million as Typhoon Bavi nears
Typhoon Bavi batters China, forcing nearly 2 million evacuations (video, Al Jazeera English)

chunks.text: A powerful storm called Typhoon Bavi has {{moved in}} on eastern China. Before it reached land, [[officials]] {{moved out}} more than 1.7 million people from towns near the coast in Zhejiang [[province]]. China's weather service {{put out}} an orange [[alert]], the second-highest warning level.

verbs.wrong: To warn people that danger is coming
verbs.correct: To make people leave a place

chunks.text: [[Out at sea]], Bavi had {{built up}} into a huge [[typhoon]] with [[winds]] near 89 miles per hour. [[On its way]], it {{passed by}} the Philippines and Taiwan, where the storm killed and hurt many people. Weather forecasters [[warned]] that it could {{knock down}} trees and [[flood]] streets when it reached the coastal city of Yuhuan late on Saturday night.

verbs.wrong: To move quickly across the ocean
verbs.correct: To slowly become bigger or stronger

verbs.wrong: To stop in a place for a short time
verbs.correct: To move past a place without stopping

verbs.wrong: To bend and twist in the strong wind

chunks.text: The typhoon {{shut down}} [[normal life]] [[across the region]]. Airlines {{called off}} [[hundreds of]] flights, and fast trains and [[ferry]] services stopped for the weekend. Officials also {{set up}} [[shelters]] where families could stay safe until the danger passed.

verbs.wrong: To force people to stay in their homes
verbs.correct: To stop something from working or being open

verbs.wrong: To move something to a later date
verbs.correct: To cancel something that was planned

verbs.wrong: To pay the cost for other people

chunks.text: Rescue teams {{teamed up}} to [[get ready for the worst]]. In Fujian province, more than 17,000 rescue workers were {{standing by}}, [[ready to help]], and the government [[promised]] millions of dollars for [[relief]]. Officials hoped that all of this [[careful planning]] would {{pay off}} and [[keep people safe]].

mainIdea.s: Typhoon Bavi built up at sea into a huge storm and moved in on eastern China. Officials moved out more than a million people and set up shelters before the storm hit land.
mainIdea.why: The story says Bavi built up into a huge typhoon, and officials moved out over 1.7 million people and set up shelters before it made landfall.

mainIdea.s: Typhoon Bavi reached China without any warning, so officials could not move people out in time. Rescue teams arrived only after the storm had already made landfall.
mainIdea.why: Close, but China issued an orange alert first and moved out 1.7 million people early, and rescue teams were standing by well before landfall.

mainIdea.s: Last spring, a separate storm flooded farmland in southern China and damaged crops for weeks. Officials there focused on fixing roads, not moving families to shelters.
mainIdea.why: This story is about Typhoon Bavi hitting eastern China in July, with evacuations and shelters, not last spring's flooding in the south.

tf.s: Only a few workers were ready to help during the storm.
tf.why: More than 17,000 rescue workers were standing by in Fujian province alone.

tf.s: Airlines called off hundreds of flights because of the storm.
tf.why: The story says airlines called off hundreds of flights for the weekend.

tf.s: Typhoon Bavi reached the coast in the middle of the day on Monday.
tf.why: The storm reached the coastal city of Yuhuan late on Saturday night, not on Monday.

tf.s: The storm passed by the Philippines and Taiwan before it reached China.
tf.why: On its way, Bavi passed by the Philippines and Taiwan, where it killed and hurt many people.

tf.s: Officials moved more than 1.7 million people away from the coast in Zhejiang before the storm arrived.
tf.why: The story says officials moved out more than 1.7 million people from towns near the coast in Zhejiang province.

tf.s: Officials refused to set up shelters, so families had to stay in their own homes.
tf.why: False. Officials set up shelters where families could stay safe until the danger passed.
